result.final_text:
## What this letter says
You went to the hospital emergency department (Emergency Department). You fell at home. You hit your head. You did not pass out (no loss of consciousness).

You had an X-ray of your right hip. It showed no broken bone (no fracture).

You had a scan of your head (CT head). It showed no bleeding inside your head.

Your blood pressure was checked lying down and again standing up. Lying down, it was 142/80. Standing up, it was 108/66. This means your blood pressure drops when you stand up (postural hypotension).

## What you need to do
1. Stop taking amlodipine 10 milligrams. It may be making your blood pressure drop when you stand.
2. Keep taking all your other medicines.
3. Stand up slowly.
4. Sit on the edge of the bed for a minute before you stand.
5. Wait for a letter from the Falls Prevention Clinic. You have been sent to them (referred). They will write to you with an appointment.
6. Your family doctor (GP) will check your blood pressure again in 4 weeks. They will check it lying down and standing up.

## Dates and medicines
- 14 October 2026: you were seen in the Emergency Department.
- In 4 weeks: your family doctor (GP) will check your blood pressure lying down and standing up. The letter does not give the exact date. It does not say who will arrange it.
- Falls Prevention Clinic: the date is not known yet. The clinic will write to you.
- Amlodipine 10 milligrams: stop taking it. The letter does not say how often you took it.
- All other medicines: keep taking them as before.

## Questions to ask your doctor
- Who will arrange my blood pressure check in 4 weeks?
- When will I hear from the Falls Prevention Clinic?
- What will happen at the Falls Prevention Clinic?

## When to get urgent help
In the next few days, call 999 or go to A&E (the hospital emergency department) if you get:
- a headache that gets worse
- vomiting (being sick)
- confusion
- drowsiness (feeling very sleepy)

If you are worried and it is not an emergency, call NHS 111. In an emergency, call 999.

---
*This explanation was made by a computer program to help you read your letter. It may contain mistakes. It does not replace your doctor, nurse or pharmacist. Always follow the letter and ask them if anything is unclear.*
